text: Imagine you are standing at a lookout above a mountain lake, on a clear and quiet morning.
Above you lies a thin blanket of air.
It presses on every square metre of you with the weight of ten tonnes, and you never feel it.
Now imagine that Earth loses its atmosphere. Not forever. For one minute.
Second one. The pressure starts to fall.
The blue sky fades to black, and the stars come out in the middle of the day.
Then everything goes silent. Sound needs air to travel.
The siren down the road is still flashing. But you hear nothing at all.
Second ten. The air in your lungs rushes out on its own.
You would have only seconds before you passed out.
But the strangest part is still to come.
Second thirty. The pressure drops below ten hectopascals.
At that point, even ice cold water boils.
The whole lake bubbles, and it loses heat so fast that its surface, and the dew on every tree, freezes over.
Second sixty. The air comes back.
The sky turns blue again, and the ice slowly melts away.
One minute without air. Do you think you would make it?
